An interpolation harness can silently split an existing entry. Appending a log section with file_editor insert at a line number that was itself computed from a stale read inserted the new section inside the previous run's paragraph, orphaning two continuation lines. Read the file tail before choosing an insertion point, or append plus reorder.

Reversing insertion order is not a load-bearing test for a tie. SQLite breaks an unordered tie by walking an index backwards, which reproduces reversed insertion - so a query with no tiebreaker looks correct. Use a fixed non-monotone permutation.

A docstring that asserts a performance property is not evidence of it. Suspect a docstring promising bounding above a select() with no where(...). NEX-086/087/088/092/094 were all this defect in different layers.

ci.yml declares concurrency group ci-<workflow>-<ref> with cancel-in-progress: true. A docs push while the product commit's runs are in flight cancels them, leaving the product commit with zero or cancelled check-runs. Read the product verdict before the docs push.

decisions_this_run: The SQL predicate lives in one named helper (_active_predicate) beside the reads, not inlined twice: two copies of a four-clause predicate are two places to drift, and the boundary test pins one.

The domain keeps is_active as the definition of 'in force' and the SQL is pinned to it by test, rather than rewriting is_active to defer to SQL. The domain must not import SQLAlchemy (enforced by tests/architecture/test_layering.py), so the arrow points adapter -> domain only.

is_active filtering moved to SQL here, reversing the earlier comment in active_for. That comment was right in principle (do not duplicate a rule) and wrong in its premise (that is_active was too irregular to translate). Each clause is a bare single-column comparison, so the translation is exact and the equivalence is now a test rather than a claim.

revoked_grants' docstring claimed is_active 'carries real logic ... which is why that filter stays in Python'. Corrected in the same commit, because left alone it would contradict the new code and re-teach the wrong rule.
